Set the contents of reader-expansion-plan.md to exactly this content:
````````````text
The existing reader carries 136 complete tests of 1,171. A read-only token census of the 1,035 excluded tests found 66 with history-related words, 42 whose first unsupported statement is a literal history declaration, 384 with solver-call words, 20 with SolverConfig words and 378 with loops. These are lexical counts, not eligibility or passing claims.

The next finite reader batch should interpret a typed, source-owned test program rather than identify prompt text. Resolve literal/constant strings, pure file fixtures, declared history constructors, reply-field references and exact assertions. Execute ordered solve and check steps, retain all native assertions, and reject the entire case when any statement, fixture helper or configuration cannot be represented faithfully. Record the source path and precise unsupported token span.

History expressions should be typed as literal text or a prior observed reply field. ConversationTurn::user and ::assistant construct explicit role/content records; solve_with_history passes that resolved history to the actual WorkerHost. A produced assistant reply must come from the actual earlier solve. A native fixture's literal assistant history stays the same literal history; it is not represented as an observed generated reply. Preserve immutable occurrence identities when a Rust binding is shadowed.

Fixture expressions can read a source-relative include_str! file within the repository, or a constant literal, or a validated pure helper match returning literals. Do not identify documented_repository_lookup by name: parse the function's declared match branches and evaluate only a supported branch. A helper's signature alone does not prove its semantics; its actual body must bind the same prompt to an available solver with mapped configuration.

Unsupported configuration must remain unsupported. For offline/default solver constructors, verify actual host semantics. Non-default repository promotion and runtime surface settings need actual browser preference/API mappings before those tests can be carried. Do not ignore configuration fields or change expected native runtime descriptions into browser descriptions.

The actual worker reply has content, intent, evidence, rawSolverEvents and derivation, but no native links_notation field. A fixture assertion on links_notation cannot be replaced by checking joined evidence or a fabricated marker. Either expose the shared canonical answer serialization from actual observed events, preserving its contract, or leave the complete case unsupported.

Closest reader contracts should use arbitrary literals, source-relative fixture bytes, produced reply references, role order, shadowed reply bindings, table iteration order and loop scopes. Include malformed fixture/helper/configuration rejection and assertion conservation. Verify parser coverage against unchanged native behavior-rule history cases, exact constant identity/unknown answers, and project language-followup cases only when all notation/configuration assertions are represented.

First finite production stage: history arrays plus literal/constant binding and checked default/offline helpers. Second stage: pure expected-fixture helpers and typed finite arrays/loops. Third stage: canonical answer serialization and explicit host settings. Keep the passing count monotonic; new carried failures must remain visible and require general source repairs, not dropped checks or fixed session outputs.
````````````
